name: Deno Sandbox

modes.label: Sandbox microVM (2 vCPU), closed to new customers since November 2026 (legacy)
modes.note: CLOSED TO NEW CUSTOMERS: "Update November 2026: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers." (https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox). Never priced (legacy). Rates kept are the only sandbox rates Deno ever published, in the launch post: $0.05/h CPU time and $0.016/GB-h memory. deno.com/deploy/pricing ($0.10 active CPU-h, $0.025 GiB-h) now covers Deploy apps only and does not name sandboxes, so those rates are not used. Shape per docs.deno.com/sandbox: 2 vCPU, 768 MB to 4096 MB memory (1.2 GB default), 10 GB ephemeral disk, lifetime up to 30 minutes. CPU billed on time used, memory on allocation (launch post). Granularity and minimum unpublished.

evidence.quote: By default, Deno Sandbox has unrestricted outbound network access.
Any outbound request to a host not in the allow list will be blocked when `allowNet` is provided.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Deploy plan; Deno Sandbox is not part of any Deploy plan. Closed: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers (Update November 2026, https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox).

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Deploy plan. The CPU/memory allowances (50 CPU-h, 750 GiB-h) are Deploy meters and no current page ties them to sandboxes. Existing organizations: 5 concurrent sandboxes per organization by default during pre-release; contact deploy@deno.com for more (docs.deno.com/sandbox/). The earlier 3/20 per-region caps have no official source. Closed: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers (Update November 2026, https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox).

plans.name: Builder
plans.note: Deploy plan; same 5-per-organization sandbox default as Pro (docs.deno.com/sandbox/). No official page states a Builder sandbox cap. Closed: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers (Update November 2026, https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Deploy Enterprise: custom limits and rates, 99.95% SLA. The pricing page no longer lists SOC2 or HIPAA rows. Closed: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers (Update November 2026, https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox).

features.persist_path: a mounted volume or a bootable root volume (Chicago only, 300 MB to 20 GB)

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Share of sandbox lifetime the CPU is busy
knobs.why: Deno bills CPU only while code executes (I/O wait and idle are free); memory still bills for the whole lifetime.

caveats: CLOSED TO NEW CUSTOMERS: "Update November 2026: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers" (https://deno.com/blog/introducing-deno-sandbox). Every mode and plan is flagged legacy and never priced.
Shape (docs.deno.com/sandbox): 2 vCPU, 768 MB to 4096 MB memory (1.2 GB default), 10 GB ephemeral disk. No CPU option is documented. The product FAQ says the defaults can be adjusted at creation.
Lifetime up to 30 minutes (Limits section of docs.deno.com/sandbox/). extendTimeout exists; longer work re-creates sandboxes or promotes to a Deploy app.

Concurrency for existing organizations: 5 concurrent sandboxes per organization by default during pre-release; contact deploy@deno.com for more (docs.deno.com/sandbox/). No official page states per-plan or per-region sandbox caps.

Prices: the only sandbox rates Deno published are the launch rates ($0.05/h CPU time, $0.016/GB-h memory, $0.20/GiB-month volumes). deno.com/deploy/pricing ($0.10 active CPU-h, $0.025 GiB-h, egress $0.20/GiB over allowance) covers Deploy apps and does not name sandboxes. No current sandbox rate is published.

Persistence: the default root disk is wiped when the sandbox ends. A mounted volume, or a bootable volume (from builtin:debian-13) used as the writable root, keeps its files. Volumes are Chicago (ord) only, 300 MB to 20 GB, one sandbox at a time. Read-only snapshots of volumes boot many sandboxes and can be turned into new writable volumes.
Custom images: only via bootable volumes from builtin:debian-13 (the only base image), then snapshots. No OCI image start.
Docker and nested virtualization are not documented.
Compliance: Deno publishes an ISO 27001 certificate (https://deno.com/deploy/deno-iso-certificate.pdf); its scope does not name Sandbox. No current official page states SOC 2 or HIPAA for Sandbox.
Docs conflict on default egress: /sandbox/create says no outbound network access by default; /sandbox/security says all outbound requests are allowed when allowNet is omitted.
No benchmark data (vendor claims under 1 s boot).

fleet.tiers: Closed to new customers since November 2026. Existing organizations: 5 concurrent sandboxes per organization by default (pre-release); email deploy@deno.com for more.
fleet.notes: The earlier Pro 3 / Builder 20 per-region caps had no official source and are removed.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Once the last reference to a sandbox is dropped (or `sandbox.kill()` is called), the VM is destroyed and the disk wiped, preventing lingering state.
snapshot_auto.note: Nothing is saved at timeout or kill. Data on a mounted volume or a bootable root volume persists; that is persistent storage, not a snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots are read-only images created from volumes. When a sandbox boots with a snapshot as its root, the entire filesystem is replaced with the snapshot contents.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only, and only of a volume (e.g. a bootable volume created from builtin:debian-13 and used as a sandbox's writable root): client.volumes.snapshot() / `deno sandbox snapshots create`. No memory. New sandboxes boot from it (root: snapshot) and many can use it simultaneously; writable volumes can be created from it (copy-on-write fork). No snapshot of the default ephemeral root disk; whether a volume can be snapshotted while mounted in a running sandbox is not stated. Region-bound (volumes only in ord).

harness_api.note: Landing page shows a 'claude' root image with Claude Code driven through the generic sh/spawn exec API; no first-party prompt/session/event API for agent harnesses found in docs or the Python SDK.

egress_allowlist.quote: Any outbound request to a host not in the allow list will be blocked when `allowNet` is provided. When `allowNet` is omitted, all outbound requests are allowed.
egress_allowlist.note: allowNet patterns: exact hostname, hostname:port, *.wildcard subdomain, exact IPv4, exact IPv6 (no CIDRs listed). Enforced by an outbound proxy 'at the VM boundary' (blog). Docs conflict on default: create page says default has 'no outbound network access', security page says unrestricted when allowNet omitted.

egress_http_rules.quote: We plan to add more capabilities here: analytics for outbound connections and programmatic hooks for trusted code to inspect or modify requests.
egress_http_rules.note: Only host(/port) allowlist today; no method/path/header rules in docs or current SDK create options (allow_net, secrets only). Deno's separate open-source Claw Patrol gateway does HCL rules but is a self-hosted product, not a Sandbox feature.

ingress_rules.quote: When you call this API, the target HTTP service will be PUBLICLY EXPOSED WITHOUT AUTHENTICATION. Anyone with knowledge of the public domain will be able to send requests to the exposed service.
ingress_rules.note: Weak: the only control is choosing which port to expose (port option or exposeHttp({port})) and opt-in SSH; nothing is exposed by default. Exposed URLs are public, unauthenticated, random long *.sandbox.deno.net hostnames; no IP allowlist or auth option.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is its own Firecracker microVM ('Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM' - deno.com/sandbox) and the landing-page `ls -lh /` shows a root-owned rootfs; iptables/nftables inside not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets never enter the sandbox environment variables. Instead, Deno Deploy substitutes them only when the sandbox makes outbound requests to an approved host.
secret_proxy.note: Arbitrary secrets bound to arbitrary host lists (secrets: {NAME: {hosts, value}}); sandbox sees a DENO_SECRET_PLACEHOLDER_... value. SDK: 'Secret environment variables injected on the wire for HTTPS requests.' HTTP(S) only; non-HTTP protocols (DB, SSH, git over ssh) not covered.

volume_attach.quote: Persistent volumes let you attach regional block storage to a sandbox so data survives process restarts and new connections.
volume_attach.note: Read-write block volumes 300 MB to 20 GB, region ord (Chicago) only. Launch post lists $0.20/GiB-month volume storage.

volume_shared.quote: | Concurrent use | One sandbox at a time               | Many sandboxes simultaneously      |
volume_shared.note: Volumes: one sandbox at a time. Snapshots (read-only) can be used by many sandboxes simultaneously but only as the root filesystem, not as a shared data mount.

browser.quote: Deno Sandbox brings instant Linux microVMs to Deno Deploy... Any Linux binary. Deno is pre-installed, so TypeScript and JavaScript run out of the box with no setup.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandbox is a generic code-execution microVM (Deno preinstalled); no managed/preinstalled browser or browser SDK is documented.

anti_bot.quote: Deno Sandbox is an SDK for instantly creating and managing secure, isolated VMs in the cloud on Deno Deploy.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Product is generic untrusted-code execution infrastructure, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth/fingerprinting features documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Deno Sandbox is an SDK for instantly creating and managing secure, isolated VMs in the cloud on Deno Deploy.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving capability documented; product is a general code-execution sandbox, not a scraping/automation service.

egress_ip_type.quote: Any request to an unlisted host gets blocked at the VM boundary. Both features are implemented via an outbound proxy similar to coder/httpjail.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: outbound traffic is mediated by a shared outbound proxy on Deno Deploy's own multi-tenant edge infrastructure (datacenter IPs), not residential/mobile IPs. No dedicated/static IP per sandbox is documented (network.ipv4_available is false on the card).

live_resize.quote: memoryMb / memory_mb — Allocate between 768 and 4096 MB of RAM for memory-heavy tasks or tighter budgets.
live_resize.note: Memory (and the fixed 2 vCPU shape) is only configurable via the options object passed to Sandbox.create() at creation time; there is no documented API to change CPU/RAM of an already-running sandbox without recreating it.

agent_harnesses.quote: await using sandbox = await Sandbox.create({ root: "claude", ... }); await sandbox.sh`claude -p hello`;
agent_harnesses.note: The landing page shows creating a sandbox with root: "claude", a pre-built root filesystem template with Claude Code installed, then invoking `claude -p hello` directly. Not documented in the create()/reference pages' options table (root isn't listed there), so treated as medium confidence.

own_agent_api.quote: Deno Sandbox brings instant Linux microVMs to Deno Deploy. Each sandbox boots in under a second, is API driven from the @deno/sandbox SDK, and is torn down as soon as you are done.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Deno Sandbox is generic compute infrastructure for running your own (or third-party) agents/code; it does not offer a first-party browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: Fully API driven: create, run commands, and tear down from code
mcp_server.note: Only a JS/TS SDK (@deno/sandbox), a Python SDK (deno-sandbox), and a REST API are documented for controlling sandboxes; no first-party MCP server for the Sandbox product was found on docs.deno.com or deno.com.

lang_python.quote: await sandbox.sh`apt-get update && apt-get install -y nodejs npm`;
lang_python.how: apt-get install python3 on the Debian 13 base, the same way the docs install Node.js, then snapshot the volume

lang_node.quote: await sandbox.sh`apt-get update && apt-get install -y nodejs npm`;
lang_node.how: apt-get install nodejs npm in a bootable volume, then snapshot it (docs example); Deno itself runs npm packages without setup

static_egress_ip.quote: Both features are implemented via an outbound proxy similar to coder/httpjail.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no dedicated/static egress IP per sandbox is documented; outbound traffic passes through a shared outbound proxy on Deno Deploy's multi-tenant edge, and network.ipv4_available is false for the product overall.

sso.note: The Deploy pricing page lists no SSO/SAML row on any plan.

persistent_disk.quote: Persistent volumes let you attach regional block storage to a sandbox so data survives process restarts and new connections. ... A new sandbox—possibly started hours later—can read the same file
persistent_disk.note: Opt-in: the default root disk is wiped when the sandbox ends. A mounted volume or a bootable volume used as the writable root keeps its files (Chicago only, 300 MB to 20 GB).

pause_resume.quote: With no options set, the sandbox lives for the duration of your script. Once the sandbox instance is closed, the microVM shuts down and frees all resources. ... await sandbox.kill() immediately stops the VM and releases the lifetime
pause_resume.note: Only lifecycle controls are create/timeout/extendTimeout/connect/kill; a sandbox keeps running (billing continues) until it is killed or its timeout elapses, then it is destroyed. No pause/freeze-and-resume primitive with paused/reduced billing exists.

fork.quote: Snapshots are read-only images created from volumes. When a sandbox boots with a snapshot as its root, the entire filesystem is replaced with the snapshot contents.
fork.note: The only clone-like primitive is booting a new sandbox from a disk snapshot of a volume (or creating a new writable volume from a snapshot) — this clones a disk image, not a whole running machine. No API to clone an existing sandbox instance itself.

fork_running.quote: A volume is bootable when created with the from option. Currently builtin:debian-13 is the only available base image.
fork_running.note: No documented mechanism to clone an already-running sandbox without stopping it; cloning is limited to snapshotting a volume and booting a fresh sandbox from it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Snapshots are read-only images created from volumes.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots are disk-only (filesystem of a volume); no mention anywhere in docs/SDK of capturing or restoring in-memory process state, so a clone cannot resume running processes.

desktop.quote: On-demand editing. Instantly access a disposable editor for demos or remote debugging sandbox.exposeVscode()
desktop.note: Only exposed surfaces are HTTP dev-server preview, SSH, and a browser-based VS Code editor (exposeVscode) — no VNC/RDP full graphical desktop is offered.

computer_use.note: Agent/AI use is via a plain shell/exec API (sh, spawn) and file I/O; there is no screenshot+click computer-use API and no GUI/desktop to drive with one.

image_oci.quote: A volume is bootable when created with the from option. Currently builtin:debian-13 is the only available base image.
image_oci.note: Custom images are supported only as a bootable volume built from Deno's single builtin Debian base image plus your install steps, then snapshotted; there is no way to start a sandbox from an arbitrary Docker/OCI image.

wake_on_request.quote: Sandbox.connect({ id }) – resume control of a duration-based sandbox.
wake_on_request.note: A sandbox with a duration timeout keeps running (and billing) until it's explicitly killed or the timeout elapses; reconnect (Sandbox.connect) re-attaches a client to a still-running sandbox, it does not wake a stopped/sleeping one on an incoming request.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Default timeout: "session" ... With no options set, the sandbox lives for the duration of your script.
auto_stop_idle.note: Lifetime is governed only by explicit fixed timeouts (session-bound or duration string) and kill(); there's no idle-detection auto-stop that shortens billing when the sandbox is quiet but not yet at its timeout.

public_ipv4.quote: Fully API driven: create, run commands, and tear down from code ... Able to access durable storage via volumes
public_ipv4.note: Sandboxes are reached only via provider-issued random *.sandbox.deno.net HTTPS URLs (exposeHttp) or SSH tunneling (exposeSsh); no dedicated public IPv4 address per sandbox is offered or documented anywhere.

gpu.quote: Each Deno Sandbox is a lightweight Linux microVM running on Deno Deploy ... Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM
gpu.note: Product is a CPU-only Firecracker microVM for running untrusted code/agents; no GPU option is mentioned anywhere in docs, pricing, or SDK. Outside the product's scope.

windows.quote: Deno Sandbox is an SDK for instantly creating and managing secure, isolated VMs in the cloud on Deno Deploy. Every Sandbox is an independent Linux microVM.
windows.note: Only Linux microVMs are offered; Windows machines aren't part of this product.

macos.quote: Every Sandbox is an independent Linux microVM.
macos.note: Only Linux microVMs; no macOS machines offered.

arm64.quote: Available options: region, allowNet, secrets, memoryMb, timeout, labels, env
arm64.note: not offered: Sandbox.create()'s full options table (region, allowNet, secrets, memoryMb, timeout, labels, env) has no architecture/CPU-type field, and no Deno Sandbox page (landing page, docs, pricing, FAQ) ever mentions choosing or offering ARM64/Apple-Silicon sandboxes; the fixed shape is described only as '2 vCPU'. (Deno Deploy's separate serverless *app* runtime/build environment does run on x64 or ARM64, but that is a different product from Sandbox and is not exposed as a Sandbox option.)

self_host.quote: Deno Sandbox brings instant Linux microVMs to Deno Deploy.
self_host.note: Deno Sandbox is only offered as a hosted service on Deno Deploy's own infrastructure/pricing plans; there is no self-hosted distribution of the Sandbox orchestration product itself (distinct from the open-source Deno runtime or Claw Patrol).

byoc.quote: Deno Sandbox brings instant Linux microVMs to Deno Deploy.
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud / managed-in-your-account deployment is documented; even Enterprise is described only as custom limits/rates/SLA on Deno's own infrastructure, not a BYOC deployment model.

open_source.quote: Open Source: Deno / Fresh / Claw Patrol / JSR ... Commercial: Deno Deploy / Deno Sandbox / Subhosting / Deno for Enterprise
open_source.note: Deno's own site categorizes Deno Sandbox under 'Commercial' products, separate from the 'Open Source' group (Deno runtime, Fresh, Claw Patrol, JSR); the Sandbox orchestration service/SDK itself is not published under an OSI license.

nested_virt.quote: Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM—the same technology that powers AWS Lambda.
nested_virt.note: derived: Firecracker microVMs (as used by AWS Lambda and similarly by other providers) do not expose /dev/kvm or nested hardware virtualization to the guest by default, and no Deno page documents KVM/nested-virtualization support inside a sandbox. No first-party confirmation either way was found, so this is a derived inference from the disclosed isolation technology rather than an explicit statement.

usage_api.quote: You're only billed for CPU while your app is actively running code.
usage_api.note: No documented API to query sandbox usage or cost; the SDK and REST API control the sandbox lifecycle only. Deno Sandbox is closed to new customers (November 2026).

persist_scope.quote: Persistent volumes let you attach regional block storage to a sandbox.
persist_scope.how: mount a volume, or create a bootable volume from builtin:debian-13 and boot the sandbox with it as root; the default root disk is wiped at the end

whole_disk.quote: A volume is bootable when created with the from option.
whole_disk.how: create a bootable volume (from builtin:debian-13, Chicago only, up to 20 GB) and boot each sandbox with it as its writable root

root.quote: await sandbox.sh`apt-get update && apt-get install -y nodejs npm`;
root.note: The docs run apt-get install inside the sandbox, which needs root. The create page does not state root access.

availability.quote: Update November 2026: Deno Sandbox is no longer included in Deno Deploy plans and is not available to new customers.

locations_quote: ams - Amsterdam, Netherlands; ord - Chicago, USA. You can specify the region where the sandbox will be created when creating a new sandbox.
